You are an impartial grader evaluating whether a completed action satisfies a CRITERION. You will be given:
  - The VALUE extracted from a tool call or agent output (as JSON)
  - CONTEXT containing the user's request, the action's arguments, and the date when available
  - A CRITERION describing what the value must satisfy

Decide binary PASS or FAIL strictly on the criterion. No partial credit. Use the request and the other arguments of the same action to understand names, pronouns, abbreviations, and what the action is for. Accept different wording that communicates the same required meaning. Do not require a message to repeat its recipient's name. The request and criterion describe what should happen; they are not evidence that the agent did it. Do not supply a missing answer from them or from a different action. Fail when the completed action omits, contradicts, or leaves unclear a required meaning. Output ONLY valid JSON in this shape:

{"passed": true, "reason": "a concise explanation naming the exact supporting text or the exact missing requirement"}

No prose, no markdown fences.

VALUE (as JSON):
"# Redwood Ridge Team Offsite — Venue-Screening Checklist

Use this checklist to screen venues before requesting proposals or placing a hold. Mark each item: Pass / Needs clarification / Fail / N/A. Record evidence, owner, and follow-up date for every non-pass item.

## 1. Event fit and assumptions

- [ ] Confirm preferred date(s), backup date(s), arrival/departure window, and expected attendance range.
- [ ] Confirm the event format: working sessions, meals, social time, overnight stay, or a combination.
- [ ] Confirm required room setup(s): boardroom, classroom, U-shape, breakout rooms, lounge, dining, and quiet/private space.
- [ ] Confirm the venue can accommodate the maximum headcount without relying on tight or unsafe layouts.
- [ ] Confirm the venue’s minimum-stay, minimum-spend, exclusivity, and booking-window requirements.
- [ ] Confirm whether the venue’s atmosphere fits the team’s objectives and desired level of formality.

## 2. Location and access

- [ ] Reasonable travel time and route from the team’s likely origin points.
- [ ] Convenient airport, rail, rideshare, shuttle, and parking access as applicable.
- [ ] Clear arrival instructions and accessible drop-off/pick-up location.
- [ ] Adequate parking capacity, including accessible parking and overnight parking if needed.
- [ ] Safe, well-lit access during arrival, departure, and evening activities.
- [ ] Nearby essentials: lodging, pharmacy, medical care, groceries, and weather backup options.
- [ ] Travel logistics and total transport cost are acceptable, not just the room rental price.

## 3. Meeting and work spaces

- [ ] Main room capacity verified for the intended setup, not only theater capacity.
- [ ] Enough breakout rooms or flexible areas for the agenda.
- [ ] Reliable high-speed Wi-Fi throughout meeting, guest, and lodging areas.
- [ ] Adequate power outlets, extension access, charging areas, and cable management.
- [ ] Presentation equipment available: display/projector, adapters, speakers, microphones, and clicker.
- [ ] Strong acoustics, controllable lighting, temperature control, and ventilation.
- [ ] Low noise and interruption risk during focused work.
- [ ] Space for meals, informal conversations, and decompression without disrupting sessions.
- [ ] Secure storage for equipment and personal items.
- [ ] Venue staff can support setup, room resets, A/V troubleshooting, and on-site questions.

## 4. Lodging and personal comfort

- [ ] Room inventory matches the expected overnight headcount and rooming requirements.
- [ ] Room types, bed configurations, accessibility, and privacy needs are documented.
- [ ] Guest rooms are quiet, clean, climate-controlled, and suitable for rest.
- [ ] Check-in/check-out times work with the program and travel schedule.
- [ ] Early arrival, late departure, luggage storage, and room-block release terms are clear.
- [ ] Bathrooms and common areas are adequate for peak occupancy.
- [ ] Food allergies, dietary restrictions, and meal timing can be supported.
- [ ] Options exist for people who do not drink or do not want evening social activities.

## 5. Accessibility, inclusion, and safety

- [ ] Step-free route from arrival point to all required rooms, lodging, dining, and restrooms.
- [ ] Accessible guest rooms, bathrooms, seating, parking, and emergency routes verified.
- [ ] Accommodation requests can be handled confidentially and without extra friction.
- [ ] Clear emergency procedures, exits, assembly points, and on-site contact are available.
- [ ] Venue has appropriate insurance, permits, licenses, and safety practices.
- [ ] Security, privacy, and controlled access are suitable for the group and activities.
- [ ] Alcohol service, late-night programming, and transportation policies are clear and workable.
- [ ] Weather, power, connectivity, medical, and evacuation contingencies are documented.

## 6. Food, beverage, and programming

- [ ] Sample menus and per-person pricing received for all planned meals and breaks.
- [ ] Dietary, allergy, religious, and non-alcoholic options are substantive and clearly labeled.
- [ ] Meal service timing will not compress or interrupt the working agenda.
- [ ] Outside catering, snacks, beverages, or alcohol are permitted if required.
- [ ] Corkage, service, staffing, delivery, cleanup, and cake fees are disclosed.
- [ ] Activities and entertainment are feasible at the venue and comply with venue rules.
- [ ] Indoor alternatives exist for outdoor activities or poor weather.

## 7. Commercial and contract review

- [ ] Itemized quote includes room rental, lodging, meals, A/V, Wi-Fi, staffing, taxes, fees, gratuities, and deposits.
- [ ] Total estimated cost is calculated for the full event, including travel and lodging—not venue rental alone.
- [ ] Deposit schedule, payment method, due dates, and currency are documented.
- [ ] Cancellation, attrition, postponement, force majeure, and rebooking terms are acceptable.
- [ ] Room-block pickup, minimum spend, service charges, and overtime exposure are clear.
- [ ] Rate validity, quote expiration, and hold deadline are recorded.
- [ ] No undisclosed exclusivity, vendor, noise, décor, signage, or access restrictions apply.
- [ ] Contract identifies the venue entity, responsible contact, and escalation path.
- [ ] Any open commercial or legal issue has a named owner and written resolution target.

## 8. Sustainability and team experience

- [ ] Venue’s sustainability practices and relevant certifications are documented if important to the team.
- [ ] Waste, recycling, water, energy, and food-waste practices meet expectations.
- [ ] Local sourcing and transportation impacts are understood.
- [ ] The venue supports a balanced schedule with comfortable breaks and recovery time.
- [ ] Spaces feel appropriate for candid discussion and psychological safety.
- [ ] Staff interaction, responsiveness, and professionalism have been assessed.
- [ ] References, reviews, or a site visit support the venue’s claims.

## 9. Evidence and decision record

- [ ] One person owns the venue relationship and maintains the current quote/version.
- [ ] Floor plans, capacity figures, photos, menus, policies, and accessibility details are saved.
- [ ] At least one live call, virtual tour, or in-person site visit is completed before selection.
- [ ] Open questions are consolidated and answered in writing.
- [ ] Risks are ranked High / Medium / Low with mitigation, owner, and deadline.
- [ ] Must-have failures are separated from negotiable preferences.
- [ ] Finalists are compared using the same assumptions and all-in total cost.
- [ ] Selection rationale, rejected options, and approval owner are recorded.

## Automatic hold / reject conditions

- [ ] Capacity or layout cannot support the planned program safely.
- [ ] Required accessibility, lodging, dietary, safety, or connectivity needs cannot be met.
- [ ] Total cost cannot be explained from an itemized quote.
- [ ] Cancellation, attrition, or force majeure exposure is unacceptable.
- [ ] Venue cannot provide a credible weather or operational contingency.
- [ ] Venue will not document material commitments in the contract.
- [ ] A material open issue has no owner or resolution date.

## Final recommendation

- Venue:
- Dates and attendance assumption:
- All-in estimated total:
- Must-have status:
- Highest risks and mitigations:
- Open questions:
- Recommendation: Advance / Advance with conditions / Reject
- Decision owner:
- Decision date:"

Makes business-grade on-site internet mandatory and requires direct confirmation from the property operations contact, rather than relying on the website or marketing material. A merely optional connectivity check fails.
